options.text: primary protein structure — The linear sequence of amino acid residues in a polypeptide.

options.label: B
options.text: secondary protein structure — The linear sequence of amino acid residues in a polypeptide.

options.label: C
options.text: isoelectric point — The linear sequence of amino acid residues in a polypeptide.

options.label: D
options.text: N-terminus — The linear sequence of amino acid residues in a polypeptide.

questions.correct_answer: primary protein structure — The linear sequence of amino acid residues in a polypeptide.
questions.explanation: primary protein structure is correctly paired with: The linear sequence of amino acid residues in a polypeptide.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes “primary protein structure”?

options.label: A
options.text: An amide bond connecting the carboxyl group of one amino acid residue to the amino group of another.

options.label: B
options.text: The linear sequence of amino acid residues in a polypeptide.

options.label: C
options.text: Local ordered folding patterns such as alpha helices and beta sheets stabilized largely by backbone hydrogen bonding.

options.label: D
options.text: A biologically functional macromolecule composed of one or more folded polypeptide chains.

questions.correct_answer: The linear sequence of amino acid residues in a polypeptide.
questions.explanation: The linear sequence of amino acid residues in a polypeptide.

questions.question: You need to distinguish “secondary protein structure” from several related chapter concepts. Which description uniquely identifies it?

options.label: A
options.text: A chain of amino acid residues linked by peptide bonds.

options.label: B
options.text: An amide bond connecting the carboxyl group of one amino acid residue to the amino group of another.

options.label: C
options.text: The end of a peptide or protein with a free or derivatized amino group.

options.label: D
options.text: Local ordered folding patterns such as alpha helices and beta sheets stabilized largely by backbone hydrogen bonding.

questions.correct_answer: Local ordered folding patterns such as alpha helices and beta sheets stabilized largely by backbone hydrogen bonding.
questions.explanation: The distinguishing description for secondary protein structure is: Local ordered folding patterns such as alpha helices and beta sheets stabilized largely by backbone hydrogen bonding.
